platform_acceptance: User confirmed all 10 usability cases passed and 10 basic points earned; version locked
source: User-provided Desktop/new_chess_log directory; all 20 JSON traces treated as data and independently replayed

comparison_to_batch01.interpretation: Both batches have 62.5% score with draw=0.5; disjoint opponent IDs and unknown opponent AI versions prevent a causal before/after strength claim.

friend.report_scope: Only the two recorded games are counted or reconstructed; the six-loss report is contextual evidence and includes unrecorded games.

independent_reference_check.method: Separate agent used recursive NumPy ref_engine minimax, without importing ai.py

early_full_margin_tt_search.method: exact-to-terminal full-window alpha-beta with fixed transposition table; unfinished searches unreported as values

earlier_terminal_wdl_proofs.method: Exact terminal WDL proof using alpha-beta window [-1,1]; bound magnitudes are not exact disc margins

hypotheses_not_implemented: Test whether mobility quality (noncorner placements and future forced captures), rather than just raw legal-move count, improves held-out middle-game decisions.
Test smooth phase interpolation: at 17 to 16 empty squares the current disc weight jumps from 2 to 10, mobility from 7 to 2, and edge from 2 to 0.
Test currently disabled stable-edge and potential-mobility terms independently against diverse held-out positions/opponents.
limitations: Only two friend replays are available; the unrecorded losses cannot be reconstructed.
The first decisive mistake has not been located. A proven already-lost position is not the cause of the loss.
Earlier unfinished terminal searches are unknown, never treated as draws or losses.
Narrow-window WDL proof signs are certified outcomes; fail-soft bound magnitudes are not exact terminal disc margins.
Observed corner ownership and mobility squeeze are symptoms, not established causal errors; late corner choices can be optimal.
No platform time telemetry is available. All 20 supplied games are terminal legal traces, but exact move/game resource usage cannot be recovered.
No candidate changes or new training were performed; ai.py remains byte-identical to the locked v12 upload.
